# transmit_heartbeat (Resource)

Pages an escalation policy when a job stops checking in. The heartbeat waits for its first ping, then opens one incident when `interval_seconds + grace_seconds` pass without another; the next ping resolves it.

Missed-heartbeat incidents are raised as the API key that created the heartbeat, so revoking that key stops its pages. A test key creates a test heartbeat. Changing the interval moves an armed deadline from the last ping, so an apply cannot hide a heartbeat that is already late.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "transmit_heartbeat" "nightly_backup" {
  name                 = "nightly-backup"
  configuration_id     = transmit_oncall_configuration.prod.id
  escalation_policy_id = transmit_oncall_escalation_policy.default.id
  interval_seconds     = 86400
  grace_seconds        = 1800
}

# Ping from the job: curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TRANSMIT_API_KEY" <ping_url>
output "backup_ping_url" {
  value = transmit_heartbeat.nightly_backup.ping_url
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `configuration_id` (String) The on-call configuration this belongs to. Changing it replaces the resource.
- `escalation_policy_id` (String) Policy in the same configuration to page on a miss.
- `interval_seconds` (Number) Expected time between pings.
- `name` (String) Unique per workspace and test/live mode.

### Optional

- `grace_seconds` (Number) Extra slack before a miss. Defaults to `300`.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `ping_url` (String) POST here with an API key holding `incidents:ingest` to check in.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import transmit_heartbeat.nightly_backup 00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000005
```
